chapter: Publishing, Jelly Roll in Los Angeles and band lore
title: Jelly Roll's arrival in Los Angeles and the Cadillac Cafe
summary: The Cadillac Cafe was on Central between Fifth and Sixth, near Spikes's own cafe; Spikes had met Jelly Roll in Oklahoma in 1912.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: time ago, so I couldn't look in the index. I was going through for material about Los Angeles to ask you about when I found your name there but it has got...uh, Jelly Roll says he came out here in a tourist car on the train. He says, "almost as dusty as a boll weevil when I arrived in Los Angeles. It was a funny situation. They had a brass band to meet me at the station but when I got off, covered in all that dust, the newcomers that didn't know me asked, 'Was that the Jelly Roll --the hot Jelly Roll--that people had talked so much about? First thing this guy needs to do is go to the cleaners,' he said. 'He's got on a dirty suit of clothes.'" And then he said it took a couple days for his clothes to get here, and so he worked in his dirty clothes at the Cadillac Cafe. Where was that?
Cadillac Cafe was on Fifth--between Fifth and Sixth on Central, and mine was at Fourth and Central.
Oh, that was very close, then.

Yeah, and Fred...and I told you I met Jelly Roll 'way back in '12 in Ariz...uh, in Oklahoma, and then he travelled with our show. We sent and got him, and then when he come out here, he went to work in the cafe about a block from my cafe.
